identity: Neutral gas-phase molecular dinitrogen tetroxide O2N-NO2, CAS 10544-72-6, singlet NO2 dimer; not liquid/reactive-fluid bulk NTO, nitrate/nitrosonium ion pairs or a different asymmetric connectivity.
recommendation: Keep current curated during this source review; a low-priority retained-thermal ATcT energy candidate can be evaluated together with NO2 when oxidizing NOx equilibria are targeted. Do not import a recent reactive-fluid equation of state as a single ideal-gas molecular standard potential.
science: ATcT lowers JANAF atomization energy by 1.691 kJ/mol, whereas NASA and modern ATcT agree to about 2 J/mol at the rounded source precision. A retained-thermal correction gives K ratio 0.873 at 1500 K and 0.950 at 4000 K. Thermal alignment changes the JANAF/NASA ratio from 0.904 to 1.009 across the range, so the small raw differences partly conceal compensating energy and thermal changes.
modern: The 2024 Polat et al. primary reactive-fluid paper was read; its partition-function sensitivities concern near-critical NO2/N2O4 phase behavior. The 2025 Samukov et al. primary NIST/publisher description and results were inspected: it combines a cubic equation of state with reaction equilibrium and VLE data near the fluid region. Neither establishes superior isolated-molecule thermal functions at 1500-4000 K. This is an explicit domain distinction, not dismissal of the newer experimental evidence.
importance: N2O4 controls NO2 association in cooler oxidizing gases and reactive fluids. The negligible current hot H-rich inventory does not validate low-temperature dimerization, liquid density or phase equilibrium.
conventions: Treat the neutral molecular dimer separately from two NO2 molecules and from a bulk dissociating fluid. Do not double count the dimer as an internal electronic or conformer state of NO2. The tabulated symmetry/torsional conventions are preserved; natural-mass evaluated functions are used without additional spin factors.
followup: If lower-temperature or oxidizing NOx modeling is needed, first extend the model domain explicitly and compare measured NO2/N2O4 equilibrium with a consistent monomer/dimer standard-state model. Within 1500-4000 K, an energy-only candidate can be built directly from existing ATcT values and tested on the current network. Neither step requires every ancestral paper before this review can merge.
